## Excursions from Santiago to Valparaiso and Viña del Mar

[Valparaiso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) are close to one another on the Pacific coast, yet they offer very different experiences. Valparaiso is known for hillside houses, its port, street architecture and historic funiculars. Viña del Mar is known for gardens, promenades and beaches.

Ada Tours offers two separate excursions departing from Santiago. Compare their actual stops when choosing: both include the same cities, but the duration and programme contents differ.

## Two available itineraries

| Programme | Distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| [Viña del Mar and Valparaiso](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-del-mar-valparaiso-tour/) | 9 hours, main city sights |
| [Valparaiso, Viña del Mar and Neruda's house](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/valparaiso-vina-neruda-full-day/) | Full day, museums and the poet's house |

The first excursion lasts 9 hours. Its price is $138, transfers are included and lunch is paid for separately. The second itinerary is described as a "full day", but no separate fixed price is specified. Do not assume its price and included services are identical to those of the first excursion.

## Nine-hour excursion: hills, the port and the Garden City

The [“Viña del Mar and Valparaiso” excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-del-mar-valparaiso-tour/) begins with a drive from Santiago through the Curacaví and Casablanca valleys. In Valparaiso, stops include Plaza Sotomayor, a walk towards Cerro Concepción and views of the port from the hillsides.

The itinerary then continues to Viña del Mar. It includes the Flower Clock, [Reñaca Beach](/chile/place/renaca-beach/), the waterfront and the Fonck Museum. Afterwards, travellers return to Santiago. There is a designated lunch stop, but food is not included in the price of this excursion.

This format suits a first introduction to both cities in one day, especially if you want to see the principal sights and know the tour's duration in advance.

## Full-day excursion including Pablo Neruda's house

The [“Valparaiso, Viña del Mar and Pablo Neruda's House” programme](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/valparaiso-vina-neruda-full-day/) also passes through the Curacaví and Casablanca valleys, historic central Valparaiso and the Garden City. It additionally includes walks along Paseo Gervasoni and Paseo Atkinson, the Fonck Museum and a visit to La Sebastiana, Pablo Neruda's house.

This version is particularly interesting for those who want a deeper insight into the coast's cultural life. The extra attraction means that time must be allocated carefully between Valparaiso's hills, Viña del Mar's museums and a walk by the sea.

The price and included services of the second itinerary are confirmed when calculating the trip. Services from the first excursion should not be assumed to be included in the second.

## How the two cities differ

Valparaiso is a port city built across steep hills. Its historic quarter has UNESCO World Heritage status. Here, the focus is on street architecture, stairways, lifts and views over the bay.

Viña del Mar reveals the resort side of the coast. The Flower Clock, waterfront and beaches offer more open seascapes. [Reñaca](/chile/place/renaca-beach/) is particularly appealing as a coastal stop, but the sightseeing itinerary does not promise independent swimming time or surfing.

Moving between the cities reveals the contrast in their urban settings. Our separate [Valparaiso and Viña del Mar destination page](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) covers their history and sights in greater detail; here, the main question is which excursion to choose.

## How to plan your coastal trip

Both itineraries require a drive from Santiago and a return to the city. During warmer summer months, the coast can attract more visitors, while the wind may pick up towards evening. Bring comfortable shoes for hills and steps, sun protection and a light windbreaker.

If museums are your main interest, check the time allocated to them and whether they will be open on your chosen date. If you want a lot of beach time, a sightseeing day with several city stops may be too busy. For an extended stay by the sea, it makes more sense to discuss a separate day.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions to Valparaiso and Viña del Mar

### Can you visit both cities in one day?

Yes. Both current Ada Tours itineraries are planned as single excursion days departing from Santiago and returning there.

### Which programme includes Pablo Neruda's house?

A visit to La Sebastiana is explicitly included in the [Neruda's house excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/valparaiso-vina-neruda-full-day/). Such a visit should not be assumed to be confirmed for the first, nine-hour excursion.

### Is lunch included in the price?

The nine-hour excursion has a lunch stop, but lunch itself is paid for separately. Terms for the other programme are calculated individually.

## Valparaiso, Viña del Mar and Pablo Neruda's house in one day

From [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), you can reach Chile's Pacific coast in a day and visit two cities with distinctly different appearances. [Valparaiso](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) is known for its colourful hillside houses, port and old lifts; Viña del Mar for promenades, gardens and beaches.

The Ada Tours excursion lasts **a full day**. After breakfast, the route passes through the Curacaví and Casablanca valleys, and travellers return to Santiago for the night. The source itinerary gives the distance from the capital to the coast as approximately **120 km**, with an estimated driving time of **1.5 hours**.

## Valparaiso: squares, hills and historic funiculars

Valparaiso developed historically as an important Pacific port. A narrow coastal plain rises into steep hills, so streets, stairs, viewpoints and historic funicular lifts have become essential parts of the urban landscape.

Our stops include **Plaza Sotomayor**, with its historic naval headquarters building. The tour then follows **Paseo Gervasoni and Paseo Atkinson** towards **Cerro Concepción**, which offers views of the port and colourful neighbourhoods.

**The historic quarter of the port city of Valparaiso** was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in **2003**. The designation refers to a defined protected historic area and its architecture, not automatically to every street in the city's modern districts.

## Viña del Mar: waterfront, beach and museum

In the second part of the day, travellers head to **Viña del Mar**. The city is known for its parks and coastal architecture; stops include the **Flower Clock**, **Reñaca Beach**, the waterfront and the **Fonck Museum**.

Including the museum and seaside stops allows you to compare the resort city with the port of Valparaiso. Here, more attention goes to beaches, pedestrian areas and the urban history of this stretch of resort coast.

There is a difference between stopping outside an attraction and making a full ticketed visit: the exact list of admission tickets has not been confirmed, so the details of the museum visit must be clarified in advance.

## Pablo Neruda's house, La Sebastiana

This excursion expressly includes a visit to **[La Sebastiana](/chile/place/la-sebastiana/)**, the house of Chilean poet Pablo Neruda in Valparaiso. The house offers a glimpse into the writer's life and the city as he saw it: from high on the hillside, the port and sea become part of the surrounding architecture.

The house museum and its visiting arrangements should be checked for the specific date. Opening hours, entry rules and photography permissions may change, and a museum ticket **must not be assumed to be included** simply because the house appears on the itinerary.

## How to allocate your travel time

The drive passes through the **Curacaví and Casablanca valleys**, with orchards, olive groves and vineyards. This is part of the overland transfer, not a separately promised wine tasting.

Valparaiso involves walking on sloping streets and stairways, and there may be a cool breeze on the coast. Comfortable shoes, a light jacket, water and sun protection are advisable. If anyone in the group finds uphill walking difficult, discuss a different pace in advance.

Other current programmes can be compared in our [Chile excursions catalogue](/chile/excursion/) or the [Culture and History section](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about the coastal excursion from Santiago

### How long does the trip last?

Ada Tours specifies **a "full day"**. The road journey to the coast is described as approximately 1.5 hours, but that is only one part of the excursion day.

### Is Pablo Neruda's house visited?

Yes. **La Sebastiana** is explicitly named in the programme. Visit times, entrance tickets and museum rules are confirmed for each booking.

### Is Reñaca Beach included?

It is on the list of sights in Viña del Mar. A separate period for swimming is not specified in the source.

### What exactly is protected by UNESCO?

World Heritage status applies to the historic quarter of the port city of Valparaiso, not the entire coastal metropolitan area.

## Tours featuring the Valparaiso, Viña del Mar and Neruda's house excursion

Our tours include the [“Valparaiso, Viña del Mar and Pablo Neruda's House” excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/valparaiso-vina-neruda-full-day/). The trip runs from [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) to the Pacific Ocean through the Curacaví and Casablanca valleys. It includes walks around the port-side hills of Valparaiso, stops in Viña del Mar and a visit to La Sebastiana.

This catalogue is designed to help you choose **a longer journey with this excursion built into its logistics**, not just a standalone excursion. In one tour, the coastal visit opens the itinerary through Chile and Argentina; in another, it comes at the end of a complex route through natural regions of Bolivia and Chile.

## Which current tours include this excursion?

### Chile and Argentina Deluxe: the excursion near the start

In the [14-day “Chile & Argentina Deluxe” tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/), the coastal day takes place on **day three**. Travellers first explore Santiago, then head west through wine-growing valleys to the cities on the Pacific coast. After returning to the capital, they fly to Puerto Natales for the Patagonian section of the itinerary.

This is a good choice if you want to begin with urban culture and coastal architecture before moving on to Torres del Paine, glaciers, the lakes of Bariloche, Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires. Here, the Valparaiso excursion provides a cultural introduction to a much larger journey.

The 14-day programme includes guide services, transfers and specified excursions, meals as outlined, accommodation and entrance tickets along the route. **International and domestic flights are paid for separately**, as are optional excursions and personal expenses. To compare offers accurately, consider the transportation component alongside the hotels.

### Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile: a cultural finale

In the [16-day “Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/), Valparaiso and Viña del Mar are scheduled on **day 14**, after Uyuni, the Atacama, Torres del Paine, San Rafael Glacier and the Marble Caves.

Here, the coastal day offers a change of scene after high-altitude journeys, boat excursions and many transfers. The day before includes a tasting at [VIK Winery](/chile/vik-winery/vik-winery-tasting-lunch-from-santiago/), and after the Valparaiso visit there is a free day in Santiago. This order suits travellers who would like to finish a long nature-focused journey with gentler cultural experiences.

The price and final services of the 16-day tour are confirmed through an individual quotation. An excursion appearing on the itinerary does not automatically guarantee a specific vehicle category, guide language or fixed price: these details are established in the offer for the selected dates.

## What you will see on the excursion day

[Valparaiso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) offer two very different visitor experiences side by side. Valparaiso is known for its port, colourful hillside buildings, stairways and historic lifts. The route names Plaza Sotomayor, walks along Paseo Gervasoni and Paseo Atkinson and the Cerro Concepción neighbourhood.

Viña del Mar looks different, with landscaped streets, the Flower Clock, waterfront and Reñaca Beach. The programme includes the Fonck Museum. A separate stop is devoted to Pablo Neruda's La Sebastiana house, which distinguishes this excursion from the shorter coastal sightseeing options.

When planning the full day, consider the return journey as well as the list of attractions. The drive from Santiago takes up a considerable portion of the day; it is better to leave the evening free after returning, particularly before a morning flight.

## Which itinerary should you choose?

| Priority | Suitable itinerary |
|---|---|
| Chile plus Argentina | Deluxe, 14 days |
| Bolivia, Atacama and Patagonia | Hidden Treasures, 16 days |
| Coastal visit near the beginning | Deluxe |
| Coastal visit near the end | Hidden Treasures |

If you only want to see [Valparaiso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) without a large multi-country journey, consider the [nine-hour sightseeing excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-del-mar-valparaiso-tour/). Its described programme is shorter, and Neruda's house is not named as a mandatory stop.

For a broader choice of programmes of different lengths, use our [Chile tours catalogue](/chile/tour/). It helps compare destinations and duration, while this selection contains only trips featuring this specific excursion module.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Pablo Neruda's house

### Which tours definitely include this excursion?

The published itineraries are the 14-day “Chile & Argentina Deluxe” and the 16-day “Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile”. Both programmes contain a separate link to the canonical excursion.

### On which day does the coastal visit take place?

It is on the third day of the 14-day tour and the fourteenth day of the 16-day one. The final sequence is confirmed when booking, taking into account flights and chosen dates.

### Can it be replaced with a shorter excursion without Neruda's house?

Any change to the programme must be arranged separately. The excursion module included in these two tours explicitly names La Sebastiana; the shortened version is a different product.

### Do travellers return to Santiago on the same day?

Yes. Both programmes describe a full-day coastal outing with a return to Santiago and an overnight stay in the capital. This excursion day does not require separate accommodation in Valparaiso.

## Valparaiso and Viña del Mar: a nine-hour excursion from Santiago

Ada Tours offers a day trip to **two distinctly different coastal cities in central Chile**. **Valparaiso** is known for its port, colourful houses on steep hillsides and historic lifts. **Viña del Mar** is distinguished by wide avenues, gardens, a promenade and the Pacific's beach-lined coastline.

The route starts in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and travels through the **Curacaví and Casablanca valleys**, where grapes and fruit crops are grown among the hills. It then visits Valparaiso and Viña del Mar before returning to the capital. **Duration: 9 hours; price: $138**. Transfers are included, while **lunch is paid for separately**. There is a stop for lunch, but food is not covered by the stated price.

## Valparaiso: a hillside city and UNESCO site

Valparaiso occupies the space between the Pacific shoreline and steep hills. Houses rise in terraces up the slopes, connected by stairways, narrow streets and historic ascensores, or funicular lifts. Its port architecture developed in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, when the city was an important link in maritime trade routes.

**Valparaiso's historic quarter was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2003.** That status applies to a specific protected area, not automatically to every building in the city. The neighbourhoods are distinctive for their combination of port infrastructure, challenging terrain, colourful facades and urban lifts.

Our itinerary includes **Plaza Sotomayor**, near the historic naval administration building. Here, the connections between the port and Chile's maritime and government history are especially apparent.

## Cerro Concepción and views over the bay

The next part of the walk is **Cerro Concepción**, one of Valparaiso's characteristic hills. Pedestrian routes wind among narrow streets and colourful houses, including **Paseo Gervasoni and Paseo Atkinson**. From viewpoints you can see the seaport, rooftops and neighbouring slopes.

In the historic neighbourhoods, street art, brightly coloured doors, stairs, old wooden cladding and a mixture of architectural traditions are easy to spot. The terrain requires comfortable shoes, however: paths can be steep, and some steps are slippery after rain.

A ride on a particular historic funicular is possible only if that lift is operating. **A ticket and ride on an ascensor are not listed among the included services**, so a sightseeing walk should not be taken as a guarantee of a lift ride.

## Viña del Mar: beaches, gardens and waterfront

After the port city, the trip continues to **Viña del Mar**. This seaside resort has parks, urban beaches and waterfront promenades. Among its well-known landmarks are the Flower Clock, Reñaca Beach and museums, including the **Fonck Museum**, with collections covering Chilean history and archaeology.

Viña del Mar looks different from Valparaiso. Its more spacious streets, resort districts and green spaces are a pleasant way to end the outing beside the ocean. Winds can be strong on the coast, and Pacific waters remain cool even in sunny weather.

The excursion confirms a visit to the city and its attractions, but **does not separately specify admission to the Fonck Museum, swimming or an extended beach stay**. If any of these activities matter to you, arrange both time and payment in advance.

## What to consider when planning

The entire programme lasts **9 hours**, so a large part of the day involves travel and sightseeing in both cities. There is a lunch stop, but travellers pay for their own meal. Confirm the starting time, meeting point and actual division of hours between port and resort stops in advance.

Coastal weather may differ from Santiago's. Cool winds, cloud and sea fog are possible, so in addition to comfortable shoes, a light jacket is useful. On the historic hills, consider the stairways and gradients if anyone has difficulty walking for long periods.

For more geographical detail, see our [“Valparaiso and Viña del Mar” destination page](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). Other cultural excursions are listed under [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Chilean coastal excursion

### What is the price and duration?

The price is **$138** and the duration is **9 hours**. The basis on which the price is charged is not specified separately, so it must not automatically be treated as a per-person price.

### Is lunch included?

**No.** There is a lunch stop, but the meal itself is paid for separately.

### What does the itinerary include?

Departure from Santiago via Curacaví and Casablanca, Valparaiso with Plaza Sotomayor and Cerro Concepción, Viña del Mar and the return transfer.

### Can you ride a historic funicular?

Valparaiso is famous for its lifts, but **boarding a particular ascensor is not confirmed** by the terms of this excursion.

### Is there time for beach relaxation?

Viña del Mar is part of the programme, but an extended swim or beach break is not separately scheduled. The length of stops is determined by the agreed itinerary.

## Tour featuring the Valparaiso and Viña del Mar excursion

The trip includes the [“Viña del Mar and Valparaiso” excursion](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/vina-del-mar-valparaiso-tour/). It lasts approximately **9 hours** and begins in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The road runs through the Curacaví and [Casablanca](/chile/place/casablanca-valley/) valleys, after which travellers explore Valparaiso's port neighbourhoods and the resort coast of Viña del Mar.

The excursion is explicitly included in the [ten-day “VIP Chile 5*” programme](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/). When choosing, bear in mind that this is **the final cultural sightseeing day** after very different landscapes across the country, not a separate multi-night beach holiday.

## How the excursion fits into “VIP Chile 5*”

The journey lasts **10 days and 9 nights**. It starts in Santiago, moves into the Atacama Desert with salt flats and high-altitude lagoons, continues to Patagonia for Torres del Paine and Grey Glacier, then returns to the capital.

| Day | Stage |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Santiago and Maipo Valley |
| 3–5 | Atacama |
| 6–7 | Patagonia |
| 8 | Return to Santiago |
| 9 | Valparaiso and Viña del Mar |
| 10 | International departure |

The seaside cities are therefore visited on **day nine**. By then, the high-altitude and Patagonian stages are complete. The coast adds historic buildings, streets and views of the Pacific, while the final stage is returning for the international flight.

One advantage of this sequence is that travellers stay at a single Santiago base before departure. But the tour includes several domestic flights, and their cost is not covered by the base services: the tour description lists flights as separately payable, with an indicative amount dependent on booking time.

## What is included in the sightseeing excursion itself?

According to the standalone excursion description, the route covers these stops:

- Plaza Sotomayor in Valparaiso and the neighbourhoods near the port.
- Paseo Gervasoni, Paseo Atkinson and Cerro Concepción, with city views.
- The Flower Clock, waterfront and Reñaca Beach in Viña del Mar.

This format highlights the contrast between the two coastal cities. On Valparaiso's hills, buildings stand at different elevations, so walking involves steps and uphill sections. Viña del Mar offers a different impression of the Pacific coast, with parks, beaches and more resort-style architecture.

Excursion terms: **transfers are included, while lunch is a separate expense**. If a particular restaurant, menu or beach stop matters, clarify it before departure. The main purpose of the nine-hour excursion is to see both cities, not to spend a long time swimming in the ocean.

## What is confirmed in the larger VIP tour?

The “VIP Chile 5*” programme includes accommodation in the stated or comparable 5-star hotels with breakfast, the specified meals, national park tickets, airport–hotel–airport transfers and excursions with transport. Round-the-clock emergency support is also specified.

However, **international and domestic flights, insurance, extra meals, voluntary tips and bank fees** are listed separately. The word VIP and the hotel category do not automatically mean that every journey uses one private vehicle or the same personal guide; check those details against your specific quotation.

Travellers interested mainly in history and architecture may prefer our [selection of cultural tours of Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/). If you want a route across the country including the desert and south, compare all the [Chile tours](/chile/tour/).

## How this excursion module differs from the Neruda's house version

The site also offers another [full excursion with a visit to La Sebastiana](/chile/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/valparaiso-vina-neruda-full-day/). It explicitly names Pablo Neruda's house museum and additional cultural stops. The two excursions overlap geographically but have different canonical IDs and programme contents.

The presence of Valparaiso on an itinerary does not, by itself, confirm a visit to the poet's house. “VIP Chile 5*” links specifically to the nine-hour sightseeing module. Before booking, rely on its own itinerary rather than importing options from the other excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about the Valparaiso and Viña del Mar tour

### Which tour features this exact nine-hour excursion?

In the current catalogue, it is the ten-day “VIP Chile 5*”. The excursion takes place on day nine of the itinerary.

### Is lunch included in the nine-hour excursion?

The standalone excursion description says that transfers are included and lunch is paid for separately. Within the package tour, the full meal arrangements should be checked against the current programme and booking confirmation.

### Will there be time to swim in the ocean?

This is a sightseeing excursion. Reñaca Beach is a stop on the itinerary, but no separate beach day or guaranteed time for swimming is promised.

### Are domestic flights required?

Yes. The ten-day VIP tour includes flight stages to the Atacama and Patagonia. They are not included in the base price and are calculated separately.

### Is Pablo Neruda's house included?

The nine-hour excursion module does not name it as a mandatory stop. To visit La Sebastiana, choose or arrange a programme that explicitly includes the museum.
